long_biography.plain_text:
American investor Daniel Loeb assembled an extensive collection of modern and contemporary art, including a substantial group of works by Martin Kippenberger. Pieces from his collection featured in the artist's retrospective at New York's Museum of Modern Art. His family's holdings have also supplied exhibitions at other museums.

With his wife Margaret, Loeb established the Ronald M. Loeb Center for Alzheimer's Disease at Mount Sinai in memory of his father. The couple's research support was recognised by the Alzheimer's Drug Discovery Foundation with its Charles Evans Award. He also endowed an undergraduate scholarship at Columbia, where he studied economics.
